summary: @bkit-plan-update returned control twice (Steps 5 and 7) while still mid-task, leaving `Verdict: PENDING` — an invalid value — at the top of plan-v2-reviewed.md and plan-v3-checked.md.
description:
@bkit-plan-update returned control twice (Steps 5 and 7) while still mid-task, leaving `Verdict: PENDING` — an invalid value — at the top of plan-v2-reviewed.md and plan-v3-checked.md. Its final message was mid-narration ("Now the ✅ commit gates for Phases 3,4,5,6" / "Now the Phase 2 tasks"). @bkit-plan-scope-check-2 did the same, returning a 20-line stub with Verdict: PENDING.

Impact: Orchestrator must verify artifacts on disk and resume the subagent; a trusting orchestrator would have recorded an invalid verdict and advanced on an unfinished plan. Cost ~2 extra resume round-trips per step.

summary: Ship Step 9: dev commit blocked by pre-commit hook
description: Ship workflow Steps 8-12 must commit docs-only changes to `dev`. The `pre-commit` hook (husky `.husky/pre-commit`) refuses commits on `dev`/`main` unless `$PWD` matches `*.worktrees/*`. Git sets hook `$PWD` to the repo working-tree root (REPO_ROOT), not the caller's cwd, so calling `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" commit` from within a worktree directory does NOT pass the `*.worktrees/*` guard. No `--no-verify` allowed.
remediation: Ship workflow Steps 9/10/Close should commit via a temp branch (`docs/ship-{FID}`) created from dev in a new temp worktree, commit there (branch != dev/main → hook allows), then FF-merge dev from REPO_ROOT. Or: add a hook exception for commit messages matching `[skip ci]`.

summary: Ship Step 5: merged PR with failing CI run
description: PR #70 was merged to dev despite CI run #26353575510 (SHA `ebcac038`) reporting `conclusion: failure`. Two root causes: (1) Step 2's `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returned a GraphQL 403 (`Resource not accessible`) due to PAT scope, silently voiding the gate; (2) repo has no branch-protection rule requiring CI pass before merge, so `gh pr merge` succeeded unconditionally. The failure itself was `Resolve Vercel URL` (infrastructure, not code); tests were skipped not failed; dev post-merge CI (`0ffd2cc3`) ran tests to success. But process gate was violated.
remediation: (1) Ship workflow Step 2 must assert `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` succeeds and ALL checks pass — treat 403 as FAIL, not skip. (2) Add branch protection on `dev` requiring CI to pass before merge. (3) After a force-push, wait for the new CI run to complete before merging (not just check whether one exists).

summary: Ship Step 8: `:\!` pathspec exclusion unsupported on macOS git
description: `git add -- ':\!.DS_Store' ':\!*.log' ...` pathspec exclusion with `:\!` prefix fails on macOS git with "fatal: bad flag in pathspec". macOS git does not support the `:\!` exclusion magic pathspec syntax.
remediation: Use explicit `git add <specific-file>` instead of exclusion-based add patterns when staging specific artifacts on macOS.

summary: Ship Step 8: worktree rebase triggered on wrong branch when switching to dev
description: Running `git checkout dev && git pull --rebase origin dev` from inside the feature worktree failed on `git checkout dev` (fatal: dev is already used by worktree at REPO_ROOT) but the subsequent `git pull --rebase origin dev` still ran on the worktree's current branch (`feat/325-multi-rule-editor`), triggering a rebase that produced add/add conflicts. The `&&` chain did not abort on the fatal checkout error because the exit code from `git checkout dev` was ignored in a subshell grouping.
remediation: Steps 8-12 must be executed from `REPO_ROOT` (the main `dev` worktree), not from the feature worktree. After merge, always `cd "$REPO_ROOT"` before any `dev` operations. Assert `git branch --show-current` = `dev` before pulling.

summary: Plan Step 3: `@bkit-plan-generate` first run wrote only a section skeleton
description: The first `@bkit-plan-generate` invocation spent its entire budget (~130K tokens, 64 tool calls, 230s) exploring the codebase and emitted `plan-v1-draft.md` as headings-only with every section reading `PENDING`; its final message was truncated mid-exploration. The Step 3.2 non-empty assertion would pass on a skeleton (file is non-empty), so the gap was caught only by an explicit `PENDING`-scan. No `SendMessage` tool is available in this harness, so the partially-progressed agent could not be resumed.
remediation: (1) Step 3.2 should scan for residual `PENDING` placeholders, not just non-empty. (2) `@bkit-plan-generate` prompt should carry a completion-first directive (write the document early, minimise exploration) — the re-invocation with that directive + seeded codebase grounding completed in 84K tokens / 4 tool calls.

summary: Build: subagents truncated during final bookkeeping (4× this run)
description: Four heavy `@bkit-build-*` subagent invocations (two `plan-execute`, one `challenge-1`, and the first `plan-execute`) each ran to ~100–120 tool calls / ~550–600s and were truncated by the harness mid-final-step — the implementation/analysis work was done but the agent was cut off while ticking plan checkboxes and writing its log verdict, leaving `Verdict: PENDING` and thin/empty findings bodies. The Step-N non-empty file assertion passes on a `PENDING` stub, so the gap is caught only by an explicit `PENDING`/verdict scan. No `SendMessage` tool exists in this harness, so the partially-progressed agents cannot be resumed (same constraint as the prior plan-generate truncation entry).
remediation: (1) `@bkit-build-plan-execute` / `@bkit-build-challenge-*` prompts should carry a completion-first directive (write the log header + verdict FIRST as a running doc, tick checkboxes incrementally) so a late truncation still leaves a usable artifact. (2) Orchestrator should scan returned artifacts for residual `Verdict: PENDING` / empty findings, not just non-empty. (3) Consider splitting plan-execute into per-task-batch invocations to stay under the per-agent ceiling.

summary: Plan Step 7: `@bkit-plan-update` emitted `Verdict: PENDING` (invalid) on plan-v3-checked.md
description: `@bkit-plan-update` completed all scope-check fixes correctly (doc-updates table added, `docs/pending.md` appended, KN entries given grep assertions) but wrote the literal `Verdict: PENDING` as the artifact's verdict header — not one of the required `PASS|CONCERNS|FAIL` values. Step 7.3's verdict-validity gate caught it. The subagent's own final report was also truncated mid-sentence (its closing narration line, not the file). Distinct from the prior truncation entries: here the _work_ was complete and the _file body_ was sound — only the verdict token was wrong.
remediation: `@bkit-plan-update` (and peers) should emit the `Verdict:`/`<!-- verdict:end -->` header as a valid value from the first write, never a `PENDING` placeholder; the orchestrator's existing verdict-validity re-invocation path handled it cleanly.

summary: Build: #403 doc edits landed inside bkit-managed blocks → push blocked by `bkit check` drift gate
description: Plan #403's Task 16/17 instructed editing `docs/deployments.md` (markers table + run-level tier table) and `docs/testing.md` (tier line) to match the new custom `bkit-decide` `ci.yml`. Those sections live INSIDE the `<!-- bkit:start -->…<!-- bkit:end -->` bkit-managed blocks (canonical, synced from `.agents/templates/`). The pre-push `pnpm bkit check` drift gate rejected the divergence and `pnpm bkit install` reverts such edits. Compounded by pre-existing dev-baseline drift (`.agents/templates/*` + `.agents/.bkit-version` stale vs installed bkit 2.8.4 — a clean `origin/dev` fails the gate too). `--no-verify` is prohibited. The design/plan/scope reviews never flagged that the target doc sections were bkit-owned.
remediation: (1) Plan/design phases must check `bkit:start…bkit:end` ownership before scoping edits to `docs/deployments.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `docs/knowledge.md`, `.agents/rules.md`, `.github/renovate.json5`; consumer/divergence content goes BELOW `bkit:end`. (2) Keep `.agents/templates` synced (`pnpm bkit install`) as part of the green-baseline check so per-PR drift doesn't surface at push.

summary: Build: rewritten ci.yml shipped an invalid GHA expression — passed every local gate, failed CI parse
description: `ci.yml` `bkit-decide` "Compute liveness and E2E gate" step used `'${{ steps.layer1.outputs.run_level == ''none'' && ''none'' || steps.layer2.outputs.run_level }}'` — doubled single-quotes inside a `${{ }}` expression, which GHA parses as empty-string + bare identifier, making the whole workflow unparseable. It passed plan-execute's gate, plan-verify, BOTH challenge rounds, challenge-tests (22 structural regex guards), and run-tests (64/64) because all of them validate via `python3 yaml.safe_load` (accepts it as a valid YAML string) — none ran a GitHub-Actions-aware linter. The line was also dead (the bash block below re-derives RUN_LEVEL).
remediation: Add `actionlint` to the local pre-push/CI gate (and to the build run-tests step) for any change touching `.github/workflows/*`. `yaml.safe_load` is necessary but NOT sufficient for workflow validation. Consider a `lint:workflows` script + a challenge-tests assertion. Especially load-bearing for a CI-rewrite PR.

step: 2 (PR CI verification) — `gh pr view 413 --json statusCheckRollup` and `gh api .../check-runs`
summary: Ship: stale `GH_TOKEN` fine-grained PAT shadowed keyring OAuth → repeated 403 on PR check status
description: `gh` resolved auth to the env `GH_TOKEN` (a `github_pat_11…` fine-grained PAT, len 93) instead of the keyring OAuth token (`gho_…`, scopes `repo,workflow,project,read:org,gist`). The fine-grained PAT lacks Checks read, so `statusCheckRollup` GraphQL and the REST `commits/{sha}/check-runs` both returned `403 Resource not accessible by personal access token`. Two same-shape failures before the workaround. (Re-logged on dev: the original entry was committed to `feat/292-recurring-caching-backend`, which was deleted at squash-merge before reaching `dev`.)
remediation: Ship workflow `gh` calls that read checks/statuses (Steps 2,3,5,12) should run with `GH_TOKEN` stripped from the environment (`env -u GH_TOKEN gh …` or `unset GH_TOKEN` at script top) so the keyring OAuth token is used. Do NOT `unset` in `.envrc` (direnv last-wins; breaks other flows). Matches memory `feedback_gh_token_stale_duplicate`.

summary: Design Step 1: GitHub MCP unavailable
description: `.mcp.json` configures `github` MCP at `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` but server returns HTTP 400 on connect; `/mcp` in-session reconnect also fails. No MCP GitHub tools loaded. Tracker writes (issue label update, comments) not possible via MCP.
remediation: Confirm `GH_MCP_TOKEN` env var is set and PAT has `copilot` scope required by the Copilot MCP endpoint. Consider fallback route via `gh` CLI when MCP tools absent.

summary: Ship Step 2: rebase conflict on feat/450-seed-fixture + statusCheckRollup PAT 403
description: (1) `git rebase --rebase-merges origin/dev` produced CONFLICT in `packages/api/tests/family-invites.integration.test.ts` and `packages/services/src/families/invite.test.ts` — not a lockfile-only conflict, so `.rebase-failed` sentinel set; Step 4 Conflict Resolve required. (2) `gh pr view 465 --json statusCheckRollup` returned GraphQL 403 (`Resource not accessible by personal access token`). Same stale-GH_TOKEN issue as the prior friction entry (2026-06-02). Fixed with `env -u GH_TOKEN gh ...` → keyring OAuth token used → Vercel checks resolved as SUCCESS; no CI GitHub Actions runs on branch (all bkit-build commits used `[skip ci]` which is by design); gate passed.
remediation: All `gh` calls in ship workflow should use `env -u GH_TOKEN gh ...` to avoid stale PAT shadowing keyring OAuth. Already suggested in prior friction entry.

summary: Plan Step 10: pre-push flake — eslint-config test timeout under parallel turbo
description: `git push` pre-push hook (`npx turbo run lint check test --filter="...[origin/dev]"`) failed twice on `@app-gether-life/eslint-config#test`. Root cause: `tooling/eslint/tests/no-inngest-in-services.test.ts` shells out to ESLint per case; under the full parallel turbo run (lint+check+test across ~10 packages) the case "rule does NOT fire for …process-message.test.ts" exceeded vitest's 5000ms per-test timeout (whole file 11.8s under load vs ~2.1s in isolation). The accompanying `*:check` ELIFECYCLE lines were collateral (turbo aborting in-flight tasks on first failure). Unrelated to this plan's docs-only changes; `test` is non-cacheable (force-executes) so plain retries did not help.
remediation: Raise `testTimeout` on the ESLint-spawning cases in `no-inngest-in-services.test.ts` (CPU-bound subprocess spawns), or cap pre-push turbo concurrency. Interim: push with `TURBO_CONCURRENCY=1` (or low value) when the machine is loaded.

summary: Build Step 5: plan-execute subagent truncated mid-run
description: `@bkit-build-plan-execute` completed the full implementation (36 files, +978) but its final turn was cut off before it ran the verification gates, ticked the plan checkboxes, or wrote the log verdict — the execute log was left a stub with `Verdict: PENDING` (Gate 5 requires no PENDING). The harness exposes no `SendMessage` tool, so the truncated agent could not be resumed in place.
remediation: For long execute passes, have the subagent write its verdict block + checkbox ticks incrementally (early) rather than only at the end, so a truncation still yields a gate-valid artifact.

summary: Build Step 5: origin/dev advanced +2 commits mid-build
description: Between worktree setup and plan-execute completion, `origin/dev` gained two unrelated merges (#468 access-history/geo, #470 supabase config). Because the bkit review/test steps consume the two-dot `git diff origin/dev..HEAD`, the drift surfaced ~21 unrelated files as reversions, and `docs/pending.md`/`docs/testing.md`/`supabase/config.toml` were edited on both sides.
remediation: Branch-sync (Step 3) only merges when `docs/` drifts; consider a full `git merge origin/dev` re-sync immediately before Build Challenge when non-docs drift is detected, so review/test always run on current dev.

summary: Ship Step 2: statusCheckRollup blocked by PAT scope
description: `gh pr view 472 --json statusCheckRollup` and `gh pr checks 472` both fail with `GraphQL: Resource not accessible by personal access token (...statusCheckRollup...)` — the fine-grained PAT lacks scope to read the GraphQL statusCheckRollup field. Gate 2 asserts on this field, which would force the Failure Path despite green CI.
remediation: Grant the PAT checks/commit-status read scope, OR have ship fall back to the REST Actions API (`gh run list --branch <head> --json headSha,conclusion`) when the GraphQL rollup is inaccessible.

summary: Ship: concurrent duplicate ship run on #290
description: A second agent ran `/bkit-ship 290` in another thread concurrently (duplicate `## Ship Workflow` Step 1 comments at 13:10 and 13:12; the local feat worktree advanced to a SHA `74539295` neither of this run's commits produced). The bkit lock did not block the second run.
remediation: Harden the Step 1 lock stale-check race (two runs read each other's not-yet-IN_PROGRESS status and both proceed); consider an atomic lock create (`set -o noclobber`).

summary: Build Step 6: origin/dev advanced +2 commits (#290/#472) mid-build
description: Between worktree setup (off dev `b795d7d8`) and plan-execute completion, `origin/dev` gained the #290 auto-bin-throttle merge (PR #472) + a follow-up. The two-dot `git diff origin/dev..HEAD` consumed by the bkit verify/challenge/test steps surfaced ~21 unrelated #290 files (auto-bin worker, `process-item.ts`, a migration, shared docs) as spurious deltas; `docs/knowledge.md`, `docs/observability.md`, `packages/services/src/workers.ts`, and the inngest-registry test were edited on both sides.
remediation: Same as the #290 entry above — a re-sync against current `origin/dev` immediately before Build Challenge whenever non-docs drift is detected.

summary: Build Step 16: slop:delta blocked push — replicated getStripe() crossed the duplicate-signature threshold
description: The pre-push `slop:delta` gate failed: the plan-mandated replicated private `getStripe(): Promise<Stripe>` (plan Q3 — deliberately NOT exported from Part-A `delete-family.ts`, to keep the reconciliation module decoupled) became the THIRD identical zero-arg `Promise<Stripe>` factory in the services package (`delete-family.ts:getStripe`, `transactions/actions.ts:getStripeClient`, mine). `structure.duplicate-function-signatures` fires at ≥3 instances, so it newly flagged all three files (`added: 3`). `dev` was green at 2.
remediation: Plan checkpoints that mandate intentional duplication (decoupled replication) should anticipate the slop dup-signature gate and pre-declare the `slop-scan.config.json` override, OR the repo should expose a single shared server-only `getStripe()` util the per-domain modules import.

summary: Build Step 16: origin/dev advanced +3 more (#290 ship cycle) during build
description: After the first mid-build rebase (onto `0bd358a4`), the #290 SHIP workflow completed and pushed 3 more commits to `origin/dev` (`update-docs-summary`, `prune-skills`, `ship DONE` → `fd1f41ee`). My branch fell 3 behind again; the two-dot review/PR diff would re-skew and a stale-base merge could regress #290's ship-phase docs.
remediation: Same as prior entries — a final re-sync against `origin/dev` immediately before push/PR whenever drift is detected (the build workflow only branch-syncs `docs/` at Step 3).

summary: Ship Step 5: GitHub stale `CONFLICTING` mergeability blocked squash-merge though git merge was clean
description: `gh pr merge 475 --squash` was rejected with _"not mergeable: the merge commit cannot be cleanly created"_; `gh pr view` reported `mergeable=CONFLICTING / mergeStateStatus=DIRTY` and `gh pr update-branch` failed with _"Cannot update PR branch due to conflicts"_. The PR head `ecb84f1e` was 27 commits behind `origin/dev` (rapid concurrent dev advancement from parallel ships). However git disagreed: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/dev origin/feat` returned a clean tree (no conflict files), and a real local `git merge origin/dev` into the actual PR head `ecb84f1e` auto-merged the 3 append-style shared docs (`.bkit/friction.md`, `docs/knowledge.md`, `docs/pending.md`) with ZERO conflicts. GitHub was holding a stale/incorrect mergeability cache, not a real content conflict. Also note: this PAT cannot read `statusCheckRollup` (GraphQL 403) or the Checks REST API (403) — PR CI status had to be verified via the Actions runs API instead.
remediation: The ship Step 2 local rebase being clean does not guarantee GitHub's server-side mergeability is fresh — Step 5 should detect a stale `CONFLICTING` (git says clean, GitHub says conflict) and force a recompute by updating the PR head, rather than routing straight to the diagnose/remediate subagent loop (whose source-edit remediation cannot fix a branch-staleness / stale-cache issue, since subagents don't push).

summary: Build Step 9-12: challenge whack-a-mole + 1-pass remediate cap forced Failure-Path fork on a trivial fix
description: The 15-spec ungate had a recurring failure CLASS (specs asserting carer/partner-only views while authed as owner; non-idempotent mutations on the shared anchor family corrupting later specs under `workers:1`). Each challenge round surfaced exactly ONE new instance the prior round missed — F1/F2 (round 1) → F8 family-leave (round 2) → family-member-rules (remediate-2 audit) → family-create-additional `active_family_id` corruption (round 3). The `CHALLENGE_REMEDIATE_ATTEMPT < 1` cap (Step 10/11) routes a 2nd FAIL straight to the Failure Path, which would have aborted the build over a one-line same-pattern fix.
remediation: (1) `@bkit-build-challenge-*` prompts should sweep the ENTIRE failure class exhaustively in round 1 (enumerate every spec/test against each defect class, not incrementally) — a single audited pass converges where N incremental rounds whack-a-mole. (2) The challenge-remediate cap should not force abort when remediation is demonstrably converging (verdict improving, failures isolated to the same class); allow a bounded extra pass under an explicit "same-class, converging" condition.

summary: Build: post-plan spec drift (#265) + FAMILY_E2E_ENABLED master kill-switch smell
description: (1) #265 merged a NEW gated E2E test (`family-child-upgrade` "upgrade via invite") AFTER the 477 plan was written; the plan's "ungate 15 Phase-1 specs" task blindly ungated it, turning a non-idempotent invite-mutation test on (409 on CI run 2). Caught only because the maintainer pointed at the commit. (2) The plan's whole design hinged on a single `FAMILY_E2E_ENABLED` master flag — exactly the mechanism that kept the suite dormant for months; maintainer directed removing it so tests run unconditionally (no flag any agent can flip to disable them).
remediation: (1) Build should re-audit an "ungate N specs" task against the CURRENT specs at build time (diff the gate set vs the plan snapshot), not trust the plan's enumeration — post-plan merges drift it. (2) Plan/design should flag a single master enable-flag gating a whole suite as a dormancy smell; prefer per-capability data-presence gates that self-resolve when data is seeded.

summary: Build Step 16: slop:delta pre-push blocked on error-obscuring catches in new e2e infra
description: Pre-push `slop:delta` (husky) rejected the push on `defensive.error-obscuring`: a bare `catch {}` in `helpers/family-seed-io.ts` (truly discarded errors) and the graceful-skip `catch (err) { console.warn(err); return }` handlers in `carer.setup.ts`/`partner.setup.ts`. The existing config already disables `defensive.empty-catch` for `apps/web/e2e/**` but not `error-obscuring`. `--no-verify` prohibited.
remediation: `@bkit-build-plan-execute` should author non-obscuring catches in test infra (bind + log the error, or use the null-returning reader), and the e2e `slop-scan.config.json` override block should cover `defensive.error-obscuring` for graceful-skip setup files from the start.

summary: Design Step 3: brainstorm subagent wrote to MAIN repo not worktree + transient rg ENOENT
description: (1) `ideate-1` reported success but wrote `design-brainstorm-ideate-1.md` to the MAIN repo logs dir (`$REPO_ROOT/docs/plans/202606/logs/454-location-enrichment/`, next to `.lock`) instead of the worktree copy — its cwd never moved into `.worktrees/454-location-enrichment` despite the `cd` instruction. Gate-3 non-empty check would have passed against the wrong tree had the orchestrator not verified worktree paths explicitly. (2) `ideate-3` hit `rg ENOENT` on every Grep/Glob and fell back to Read-only of docs/\*.md; the binary is actually present (ripgrep 14.1.1, wrapped via the claude shim) so this was transient/env-specific to that subagent shell, not a real outage. Its key finding (entitlement model already exists) was still correctly grounded via Read of `docs/data-schema.md:546`.
remediation: Orchestrator should verify each parallel subagent artifact at its WORKTREE path (not trust the subagent's reported absolute path) and relocate stragglers before the gate. Brainstorm subagent prompt could assert `pwd` ends in the worktree before any Write. The rg-shim flakiness in subagent shells is worth a bkit-upstream note if it recurs.

summary: Plan Step 5: apply-review subagent emitted invalid `Verdict: PENDING`
description: `bkit-plan-update` resolved all 4 CRITICAL review findings into `plan-v2-reviewed.md` but left the verdict header as `Verdict: PENDING` (mid-deliberation between PASS and applying a last OPTIONAL). Step 5.3 requires `PASS|CONCERNS|FAIL`; PENDING is invalid → mandates re-invoking the offending subagent to re-emit only the verdict. The prescribed recovery path uses `SendMessage` to continue the same agent, but `SendMessage` is NOT available as a callable tool in this harness (only referenced in the Agent tool description) — so the same agent could not be continued with context intact.
remediation: (1) `@bkit-plan-update` should finalise the verdict header (never leave PENDING) before returning. (2) The plan workflow's verdict-fix sub-step assumes `SendMessage`; where unavailable, spawning a fresh same-type subagent with a narrow "re-emit verdict only, do not redo work" instruction is the faithful substitute and should be documented as the fallback.

summary: Design Step 4: generate subagent repeatedly hit API 529 Overloaded
description: The `@bkit-design-generate` subagent died with `API Error: 529 Overloaded` on four consecutive spawns (initial + 3 retries). The first attempt did 20 tool calls (repo exploration) but wrote nothing before dying; later attempts 529'd with 0 tool uses. This was a sustained server-side Anthropic API incident (~25 min), not a workflow fault — all prior design state (input + 3 brainstorms) was already committed on `feat/478-sentry-observability`, so nothing was lost. A 529 is NOT a real step/tool/gate failure, so the bkit Failure Path (which marks `bkit:failed` + posts a failure comment) was deliberately NOT triggered.
remediation: For transient `529 Overloaded` on a subagent spawn, the orchestrator should back off (escalating: ~4m → 10m → 20m via a detached background `sleep` that re-invokes on completion) and retry the same step, rather than routing to the Failure Path. The Failure Path should be reserved for genuine work failures (bad verdicts, missing artifacts, gate violations), not infrastructure overload. Re-spawning fresh is fine here because the brainstorm artifacts already carry the repo exploration the generate step needs.

summary: Plan Step 1: divergence guard blocked on unpushed dev commit → human-confirm prompt
description: Step 1's divergence guard (`git rev-list --count origin/dev..dev`) found local `dev` 1 commit ahead of `origin/dev` (`2aba4de4` — a one-line ci.yml rename of a CI check label) and exited non-zero, which the protocol maps to the Failure Path. Routing to the Failure Path here would have been wrong: no plan workflow state existed yet (no worktree, no plan status, lock not yet held), and it would have stamped `bkit:failed` on #478 for a trivial "your local dev is unpushed" condition. The blocker also fell into the reserve-stop "CI edits" category (pushing the commit triggers a CI run on dev), so I surfaced it rather than unilaterally pushing.
remediation: The Step 1 divergence guard should distinguish "local dev ahead by unpushed commits" (a benign, user-resolvable precondition) from a genuine workflow failure — emit a clear blocker + offer to push/override instead of mapping straight to the Failure Path (which mislabels the issue). A pre-Step-1 `git status` summary of unpushed dev commits would let the human decide in one prompt.

summary: Design Step 4: generate subagent wrote out-of-scope `docs/pending.md`
description: `@bkit-design-generate` recorded two deferred follow-ups (Approach R analogue; RSC complement) by appending to `docs/pending.md`. The design phase scope is "output lives in `docs/plans/` only", and the design close-workflow STRAY guard allows ONLY `^docs/plans/|^\.bkit/friction\.md$` — so a `docs/pending.md` edit would `exit 1` the squash-merge at Step 10. The follow-ups are also premature at design time (pending.md is updated at SHIP). Their rationale is already fully captured in the design doc (D2, Approaches Considered, the OUT-OF-SCOPE Approach-R row line 214).
remediation: design subagents should keep deferred/backlog items inside the design doc's Decisions / Approaches-Considered, never touch `docs/pending.md` (that is a ship-phase artifact). Alternatively the design close STRAY guard could whitelist `docs/pending.md`/`docs/decisions.md` (cf. the known plan-phase variant of this gotcha).

summary: Build Step 5: plan-prescribed client-side `convertItemType` call is ESLint-boundary-illegal → remediation round
description: `293-item-popover-crud-plan-3.md` task 3.2 (and design amendment 10) specify "`useItemForm` calls `convertItemType()` and prepends the preamble to `description` on Save" — i.e. a CLIENT-side call. But `convertItemType` lives in `@app-gether-life/services`, and the shared ESLint config (`tooling/eslint/eslint.config.js` ~L26-79) enforces `boundaries/element-types` + `no-restricted-imports` that forbid ANY UI layer — both `packages/ui` and the `"use client"` host `apps/web/.../index-list.tsx` — from importing `@app-gether-life/services`. The first execute pass tried to honour the plan via an optional `getPreamble` prop injected by the host, but there is no legal client injection point, so it shipped as dead JSDoc. A correction round moved preamble application server-side into `updateItem` (services→services import is legal, DB-authoritative) and removed the dead prop.

summary: Build Step 5 (sub-plan 1): execute subagent budget-capped at PENDING; missed web-level type integration check
description: `@bkit-build-plan-execute` for Child 1 (WS-1…WS-5, 20 tasks) implemented all tasks but hit its tool/context budget (~116K tokens, 117 tool-uses) before ticking checkboxes/finalising — returned `Verdict: PENDING` (invalid for Gate 5). Worse, it ran only **per-package** `tsc` (which passed in isolation) and never the **web-level** typecheck, so it missed a real TS2345: the scrub helper's inline `SentryEvent`/`SentryBreadcrumb` types (with `[key:string]: unknown` index signatures) were not bidirectionally assignable to Sentry's real `ErrorEvent`/`Breadcrumb`, so `...sharedSentryConfig` spread into `Sentry.init()` failed `web check:type`. remediation: (a) build subagents should run the **consumer-level** typecheck (`turbo check:type --filter=web`) for any shared-package change consumed by the app, not just the package's own `tsc --noEmit` — isolated per-package tsc green is necessary-not-sufficient when a downstream app spreads the export into a typed 3rd-party API. (b) Right-size 20-task children OR raise the execute budget so a single pass finishes the runbook + checkbox ticking. (c) For Sentry scrub hooks, type from `@sentry/core` (`import type`, erased) rather than hand-rolled inline shapes — the inline shapes can't be both test-fixture-ergonomic and `Sentry.init`-assignable.

summary: Build Step 12 (challenge-tests): cross-sub-plan test regression — sub-plan 2 getClient() broke sub-plan 1's mock
description: Sub-plan 2 Task 6.1 added a boot-time `Sentry.getClient()` assertion to `apps/web/sentry.server.config.ts`. Sub-plan 1's `apps/web/instrumentation.test.ts` (Task 4.4) imports that config and mocks `@sentry/nextjs` with only the exports it needed at sub-plan-1 time (`init`/`captureConsoleIntegration`/`captureRequestError`) — no `getClient`. Neither the Step 8 holistic verify nor the sub-plan-2 verify caught it because they ran `check:type --filter=web` + `next build` but NOT the web vitest unit suite; it surfaced only when the Step-12 challenge-tests subagent ran `pnpm --filter web test`. The challenge-tests subagent mis-labeled it "pre-existing, unrelated" — it is this feature's own test.
remediation: when a later sub-plan changes a module that an earlier sub-plan's TEST imports/mocks, the holistic verify (Step 8) should run the affected package's UNIT SUITE, not just typecheck/build — a mock missing a newly-added named export is invisible to tsc (the real module type-checks; the mock is `() => ({...})` untyped). Consider a typed mock or `importOriginal` partial mock so a missing export fails at type-check.

summary: Plan Steps 5–7: apply-\* subagent edited only the expanded plan copy, leaving the `bkit:start…bkit:end` canonical mirror stale → self-contradicting plan, full reconciliation pass

summary: Slop delta pre-push failure: error-obscuring catch blocks from URL parsing
description: Pre-push `slop:delta` gate blocked push with 3 added / 2 resolved → net +1 finding. Two net-new findings were `defensive.error-obscuring` on `try { new URL(s); ... } catch { return null/false }` in `domain-filter.ts:26` and `match-chunks.ts:194`. These catch blocks silently swallow URL parse errors and return default values, which slop-scan classifies as error-obscuring (boundary=none). Third finding in `chat-widget.tsx` was net-zero (old `as any` moved, new `as any` added at same score).
remediation: When adding URL parsing helpers, prefer regex hostname extraction (`/^https?:\/\/([^/?#:]+)/i.exec(url)?.[1]`) over `try { new URL(); } catch { return null }` to avoid the error-obscuring pattern. The regex approach is valid for well-structured HTTP/HTTPS URLs from known sources (corpus, operator websites).

description: `pnpm bkit upgrade --latest` (and `--to=<v>`) — bkit's documented supported way to move versions — aborts with ERR_PNPM_ADDING_TO_ROOT in any pnpm-workspace consumer. The wrapper runs `pnpm add -D @cbartens/bkit@<v>` WITHOUT the -w/--workspace-root flag, which pnpm refuses when the dep lives in the workspace-root package.json. Nothing re-renders; the version never bumps (exit 1).
remediation: bkit upgrade should pass -w (or set ignore-workspace-root-check) when @cbartens/bkit is a workspace-root dep. Consumer workaround: `pnpm add -D -w @cbartens/bkit@<v>` then `pnpm bkit upgrade` (no version flag) to re-render + re-pin from the freshly-installed binary.

description: bkit check tier2-text-drift flags the managed main-lag-warning block in a CUSTOM full-scaffold ci.yml as drifted because the 4.3.0 template hard-codes `if: steps.cache.outputs.skip != 'true' && …` on the 'Check Main Lags Dev' step. That steps.cache.outputs.skip reference exists ONLY in the STARTER ci.yml (which ships a 'Check SHA Cache' step id: cache); a full-scaffold consumer has no such step (0 occurrences). Re-syncing per the advisory injects a reference to an undefined step id, which the Run Actionlint CI gate rejects — following the advisory breaks CI.

Until upstream-fixed, the orchestrator overrides the guard for `docs/pending.md`/`docs/decisions.md` ONLY (never `--no-verify`, never dropping content).

description: @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-queue with `Verdict: PENDING` still in the header after ~50 tool calls, having applied 10 of 14 findings. The artifact looked complete (105KB, full structure, coherent tail), so the orchestrator spot-checked four findings (A, B, D, G-atomicity), found them landed, and resumed the agent with `Do NOT redo work` + a verdict-only instruction. That premise was WRONG: findings F (CRITICAL, would red bkit-tests-check on every run), G-mirror (CRITICAL), M1 and M5 were still unapplied. The subagent audited on-disk state, rejected the orchestrator premise, finished the four, and only then emitted PASS.
recovery: Subagent self-corrected — it refused to certify PASS over an unapplied CRITICAL and completed the queue instead of obeying the (wrong) do-not-redo instruction. Orchestrator re-verified the late fixes against live source (the 9-key env enumeration matches ci.yml:879-888 exactly) and confirmed the commit captured the completed state. No rework lost; no bad verdict shipped.
lesson: A PENDING verdict means the agent did not finish its QUEUE, not merely its header — the artifact being large, well-structured and coherent is NOT evidence the finding queue drained. The Step 5.3 `Do NOT redo work` re-emit instruction is only safe once EVERY finding is confirmed applied; a 4-of-14 spot-check cannot establish that. Either verify all findings before re-emitting, or resume WITHOUT the do-not-redo constraint and let the agent audit its own queue.

description: REPLAN into an existing FID reuses docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ — every artifact from the prior (closed, merged-to-dev) run is already on disk. Subagents whose Create target already existed partially rewrote it instead of replacing it, silently carrying superseded content into the new round. @bkit-plan-summary produced a summary whose top half was correct (new Findings A/B) but whose bottom half was v4 carry-over: it presented 'T3a — Cancellation Data-Safety Scope' and 'T17 — P4 Lane Balance' as THE TWO OPEN HUMAN DECISIONS — i.e. the exact two items (item 1, item 6) the maintainer had explicitly DROPPED in the AGREED SCOPE comment — plus retired T10a, dead 3-runner-matrix/shard framing, and a non-existent 'defer item 6 -> 7 of 8' option. plan-summary.md is displayed VERBATIM to the maintainer as the plan-phase output, so this would have actively misrepresented the plan at the decision point. Reviewers 2/3 and scope-check-1 hit the same class and self-reported resetting stale files to a stub before writing; the summary agent did not.
recovery: Orchestrator diagnosed by checking the artifact against the dev copy (git show dev:<path> | grep -cE 'T17|shard|item 6' = 20 stale matches), rejected the artifact despite its VALID 'Verdict: PASS' header, and resumed the agent with an explicit purge list (retired IDs T0a/T3a/T3/T7-T12/T10a/T17-T21; live IDs enumerated) plus an instruction to rewrite from the current artifacts ONLY, keeping the genuinely-new top half.
lesson: A valid verdict header is NOT evidence the artifact is current — on a REPLAN the dangerous failure is stale CONTENT under a fresh-looking header, which no gate checks (gates test for PENDING placeholders, not supersession). Two mitigations: (1) on replan into an existing FID, have each subagent reset its Create target to a stub before writing, or archive the prior round to logs/{FID}/superseded-{N}/ at plan start; (2) the orchestrator must grep every artifact for known-retired identifiers before accepting it. The cheap check that caught this: grep -cE '<retired-ids>' <artifact>.

description: @bkit-plan-summary needed FOUR orchestrator round-trips to converge: (1) initial output was stale-v4 contaminated (logged separately); (2) rewrite was clean but carried 6 factual errors (PR2 described as a 'sequential shell' — contradicting PR 2's entire purpose; PR 4 mislabelled as item 8 when item 8 is assertLiveEnv/PR 1; global.teardown.ts line numbers attributed to playwright.config.ts; 'three critical errors' heading five; understated ledger counts); (3) five of six landed, ledger counts still wrong; (4) even after being handed the exact enumerated keys and counts, the agent's own completion report AGAIN said 'Deferrals 3 rows' and the file still read 3 — the true value was 9. It self-corrected on a second internal pass only after the orchestrator moved to edit the line directly (the Edit collided with the agent's write).
recovery: Orchestrator verified every claim against ground truth rather than the agent's report — `git diff dev --numstat` on both ledgers gave 3/0 and 9/0, contradicting the agent's '1 new row' and '3 rows'. After the 3rd same-shape failure on one number, applied the repo's own structural-fix-before-retry rule and moved to fix it directly; the agent landed it concurrently. Final state verified correct on disk (3/0, 9/0), all six corrections in, zero stale markers.
lesson: A subagent's completion report is not evidence — this agent reported success on a value that was still wrong in the file, twice. Always diff the CLAIM against ground truth (`git diff --numstat`, a grep count), never against the agent's prose. Second: an anchored numeric fact resists correction even when the exact value is supplied verbatim; after 2 same-shape failures on a trivial converging fix, editing the one line directly is cheaper and more reliable than a 4th delegation round — the no-inlining rule targets doing the subagent's ANALYTICAL work, not a one-token factual repair. Third: plan-summary ships VERBATIM to the maintainer, so it warrants a full read + fact-check, not a gate check.

description: bkit-build Step 5 (Sub-Plan Loop) hard-conflicts with a plan that bkit-plan's own complexity-split produced. plan-complexity-split partitioned #681 along its OWN 'Merge Method' axis into four independently-mergeable, merge-gated PRs (master plan: 'always squash. Four independently-mergeable PRs, each its own squash into dev'; PR 2 requires PR 1 merged; PR 3 sequenced after PR 2; PR 4 requires PR 1 merged), and each sub-plan gate terminates in an OBSERVED REAL CI RUN validated against the POST-MERGE dev state. bkit-build has no notion of a merge boundary between sub-plans: the loop runs SUB_PLAN 1..SUB_COUNT on ONE worktree branch and Step 17 raises exactly ONE PR. Executing the loop literally would have made every PR 2/3/4 gate unsatisfiable (cannot observe a CI run against a dev that never received PR 1) and landed ~22 tasks of ci.yml edits as one diff. plan-summary's Recommended Next Step is a bare '/bkit-build 681', which gives no signal that the run must be scoped to one sub-plan.
recovery: Orchestrator read the four sub-plan headers + the master Merge Method table BEFORE invoking @bkit-build-plan-execute, detected the fork, and stopped to ask the maintainer directly (repo rule: reserve stops for arch forks / CI-edits; both applied). Maintainer selected 'PR 1 only this run'. Run scoped to SUB_COUNT=1 / SUB_PLAN=1 against 681-ci-speedup-plan-1.md; sub-plans 2-4 logged as OPEN deferral rows in docs/deferrals.jsonl (keys pending-681-sub-plan-{2,3,4}-deferred-to-own-build-run); Step 8 holistic verify skipped as meaningless for a single sub-plan.
lesson: When plan-complexity-split partitions along a MERGE-boundary axis, the resulting sub-plans are NOT slices of one PR, and bkit-build cannot execute them in one run — the two workflows disagree about what a sub-plan IS. Detect at Step 5 by reading the sub-plan headers and the master Merge Method table before any executor is invoked; the tell is a precondition phrased as 'PR N must be squash-merged to dev', or a gate requiring an observed CI run. Two upstream fixes: (1) plan-complexity-split should mark a merge-gated split so bkit-build can scope one sub-plan per run and plan-summary can emit '/bkit-build 681 --sub-plan 1' instead of a bare invocation; (2) bkit-build Step 2 should surface a merge-boundary precondition as a first-class gate rather than relying on the orchestrator noticing.

description: Orchestrator self-inflicted a wasted CI cycle. While run 29454200201 (the first real test of THREE unproven changes at once — node_modules cache removal, sequential E2E lanes, and @live running parallel to e2e) was in flight and being actively monitored, the orchestrator committed and pushed a DOCS-ONLY change (a failures.jsonl ledger row). The PR's concurrency group cancelled 29454200201 mid-run and started 29454436704 on the new HEAD. Net effect: ~10 minutes of CI wall-clock burned for nothing, on a branch whose entire purpose is REDUCING CI wall-clock, and the awaited measurement was delayed by a full cycle. The push itself was not wrong — the ledger row and the #681 correction comment were both worth recording — the error was pushing it DURING an in-flight run instead of holding it until the run reported, or batching it into the next code push.
recovery: None available — a cancelled run cannot be resumed. The new run 29454436704 carries the identical tree plus the docs row, so the measurement is delayed rather than lost. Re-pointed the monitor at the new run id.
lesson: Never push to a branch while a run you are waiting on is in flight — a PR push cancels the in-progress run via the concurrency group. Ledger/docs writes that are not needed by CI should be held in the working tree (or committed but NOT pushed) until the awaited run reports, then batched with the next real change. This matters most in exactly this situation: several unproven changes landing together, where the pending run is the only thing that can tell you which of them works. Cheap check before any `git push`: `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json status` — if it is in_progress and you care about its result, wait.

description: Four subagents terminated mid-flight and had to be resumed: @bkit-plan-generate (soft-truncated its final message), @bkit-plan-update apply-review (API error 'Connection closed mid-response'), @bkit-plan-scope-check-2 (stopped with NO artifact on disk at all), @bkit-plan-update apply-scope (stopped mid-edit of the ledger sub-header). In three of the four cases the agent left an artifact that looked plausible but carried 'Verdict: PENDING' at line 1 — a completion claim the workflow gate would reject. scope-check-2 wrote nothing despite reporting verification work in-context.
recovery: Orchestrator verified every artifact on disk (line count, verdict header, PENDING grep, git status, ledger numstat) before accepting any subagent completion claim, per the repo rule 'verify subagent artifact before trusting completion'. Each cut-off agent was resumed via SendMessage with its context intact rather than restarted from scratch — resumes were given an explicit inventory of what was already verified done (so they would not redo work), an explicit list of what remained, and a mandatory 'cd back into the worktree, verify with pwd' first instruction (resumed agents can lose cwd). All four resumed cleanly and completed; zero work lost, no restarts needed.
lesson: A subagent's final message is not evidence of completion — three of four cut-off agents left a plausible-looking artifact stamped 'Verdict: PENDING', and one left no file at all while reporting progress. Always check disk. Resume-with-inventory (naming what is verified-done and what remains) is materially cheaper than re-running a 150K-token subagent, and preserved correctness across all four incidents here.

summary: Debug Step 2 aborts the entire workflow on any non-pnpm-lock rebase conflict. Here the conflict was a single ADDITIVE doc-line collision in docs/architecture.md (dev cd34b6060 marked G7 closed by #839; branch 5ada057fc inserted the #836 G11 sentence into the same Index/Dashboard bullet) — trivially resolvable, but it hard-stopped a debug run that had not yet even looked at the reported e2e CI failure.
description: Step 2 auto-resolution only special-cases CONFLICT_FILES == pnpm-lock.yaml. Long-lived bkit feature branches accumulate docs/architecture.md + docs/testing.md + docs/navigation.md edits from plan-execute commits, and concurrent issues (here #839, #860) edit the same summary bullets on dev, so same-line doc collisions are the common case, not the rare one. Secondary defect observed in the same block: the else-branch runs `git rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true`, whose silenced stderr hid that the abort did NOT land — the worktree was left mid-rebase at commit 8/22 with a UU file and HEAD detached at 194175466, and only a manual re-run of `git rebase --abort` with visible stderr restored HEAD to 47bdbdcf8. Additionally the Failure Path block appends the workflow-failed row to status.jsonl BEFORE running `git rebase --abort`, so on a mid-rebase abort the append is discarded by the abort; orchestrator inverted the order to preserve the record.
remediation: Orchestrator aborted cleanly, verified HEAD == origin/feat/836-universal-ui-gaps, released the lock, and routed to the Failure Path with a handover documenting the exact three-way resolution. Suggested bkit changes: (1) extend the Step 2 auto-resolution allow-list to docs-only conflicts under docs/ (or add a bkit-ship-conflict-resolve-style subagent hop before declaring failure), (2) drop the 2>/dev/null on the rebase --abort calls and assert the rebase dir is gone afterwards, (3) move the workflow-failed status append AFTER the abort in the Failure Path.
source: bkit-debug orchestrator, #836 debug attempt 1, Step 2 sub-step 3

summary: Step 3 regression guard FAILs on a conflicting branch whose tip commit never triggered CI
description: Ship Step 3 resolves CURRENT_RUN_ID from the PR head SHA and FAILs when empty. A docs-only tip commit that CI path-filters away leaves the PR head with zero runs, so the guard FAILs even though the prior commit is green. Step 3 also runs BEFORE Step 4 conflict-resolve, so on a branch that must be rebased + force-pushed the guard evaluates a head that is about to be discarded.
remediation: Order Step 3 after Step 4 when the .rebase-failed sentinel is present, or treat empty CURRENT_RUN_ID as DEFER (re-evaluate post-rebase) rather than FAIL. Step 6 sub-step 4 already independently blocks merge on CI completed+success at the real PR head, so the safety property does not depend on Step 3.

summary: Ship Step 10 commits with a blanket `git add -- docs/`, swallowing a concurrent session staged work in the shared main checkout
description: Step 10 runs `git add -- docs/ && git commit -m docs({FID}): update-docs-summary -- docs/` in REPO_ROOT. When another bkit workflow is running against the same main checkout it may already have content staged under docs/. Observed live: a concurrent bkit-plan 837 plan-amend had staged docs/deferrals.jsonl plus six 837 plan files; the prescribed command would have committed them under this FID message, misattributing another feature work and detaching it from its own workflow commit.
remediation: Scope the Step 10 commit to the paths this run actually changed (the FID log dir plus the specific doc files ship-update-docs reports editing) instead of the whole docs/ tree, or snapshot `git diff --cached --name-only` before the step and refuse to stage anything not attributable to this FID.

summary: bkit worktree setup does not copy apps/mobile/.env.local, so EXPO_TOKEN is absent in the worktree and every eas command fails
detail: The Step 2 env-copy loop covers .env, .env.local, apps/web/.env.preview and apps/web/.env.production only. EXPO_TOKEN lives in apps/mobile/.env.local (named as its home by ci.yml:2849). Sub-plan 2 pre-flight requires a live `eas env:list` and `eas build:view`, both of which need it. Also had to `direnv allow` the worktree .envrc (blocked on a fresh worktree) and `npm i -g eas-cli@21.4.0` since eas-cli is deliberately never a workspace dependency (ci.yml:2854).

summary: a truncated subagent leaves the PREVIOUS build run artifact in place, and the bkit non-empty gate passes it — a stale "Verdict: PASS" is read as this run verdict
detail: Three subagents were cut off mid-run in this build (build-plan-execute, build-challenge-remediate, build-challenge-tests). Each left the artifact from the previous build run on disk, byte-identical to HEAD, each carrying sub-plan 1 "Verdict: PASS". The orchestrator gate specified in .claude/commands/bkit-build.md is "assert Update/Create files exist, are non-empty" — all three stale files passed it. Detected only because the orchestrator ran `git diff --quiet <artifact>` and grepped for run-specific tokens; without that, a stale PASS would have been recorded as this run verdict and the workflow would have advanced on it. build-plan-execute additionally wrote a 71-byte "Verdict: PENDING" stub, which the gate own "No PENDING placeholders remain" check would catch, but the other two produced no new bytes at all so nothing flagged them.
remediation: strengthen the artifact gate from exists+non-empty to also require the file be modified relative to HEAD (git diff --quiet <path> must FAIL) whenever the step is expected to (re)write it; for log dirs carried across runs, prefer per-run filenames or have the orchestrator delete the prior artifact before invoking the subagent

summary: running eas from the repo ROOT (not apps/mobile) silently recreates the stub root app.json that #886 commit 587dc0116 deliberately deleted; git add -A in a bkit worktree would resurrect it
detail: During #712 sub-plan 2 several agents invoked eas (env:list, build:view, build:list) to settle plan pre-flight questions. eas writes a stub {"expo": {}} app.json into its cwd when it cannot find one, so a call made from the repo root recreated the exact 16-byte file that fix(886) 587dc0116 removed as "the stub root app.json swept in by 173d025af". It arrives UNTRACKED, so it survives every gate and the bkit-build per-step `git add -A` (legal in a dedicated worktree) would have committed it. Caught by reading git status before the commit, not by any gate.
remediation: always cd apps/mobile before any eas invocation (that is where eas.json and the real app.json live); consider adding /app.json to .gitignore so a stray stub can never be staged, since the root app.json is intentionally absent

summary: bkit worktree setup copies .env/.env.local/apps/web/.env.preview/.env.production but NOT apps/mobile/.env.local, so eas is unauthenticated in every worktree

The Step 2 copy loop in .claude/commands/bkit-build.md does not include that path, so `npx eas whoami` in a fresh worktree returns `Not logged in` and every eas-dependent task fails on auth rather than on its real assertion. Orchestrator copied the file manually; it is gitignored (apps/mobile/.gitignore:33 `.env*.local`) so it cannot be staged.

summary: orchestrator build-input granted a second metered-run allowance the sub-plan's own Rollback Strategy did not budget, so a compliant subagent over-spent while believing it was following the plan
description: Sub-plan 4's Rollback Strategy (712-native-e2e-harness-plan-4.md:119) budgets exactly ONE metered maestro run: "bounded to a single maestro invocation". The Step 5 build input for this sub-plan (docs/plans/202607/logs/712-native-e2e-harness/build-input.md, Task 13 Pre-Flight, CAUTION callout) instead reads: "Run it once. Do not loop, do not retry-on-a-whim; if the first run is inconclusive for an environmental reason, say so explicitly in the log before spending a second." That sentence grants a conditional second-run allowance the plan text itself never contains. The build-plan-execute subagent took the allowance, spent a second real (metered) run, and cited it in its log as coming from "Task 13's Money section" and "the sub-plan's one-additional-run allowance" — a misattribution (the real source is the orchestrator prompt, not plan text) caught by build-plan-verify as GAP 2. The overspend itself was disclosed honestly (both run ids logged) and produced a real finding (flow_path is relative to the app's own base dir, not the repo root), but the budget mismatch between plan text and orchestrator prompt is the root cause, not the subagent.
remediation: When an orchestrator step prompt (build-input.md or an inline Step N instruction) grants a spend/retry allowance beyond what the sub-plan's own Rollback Strategy or Money/budget language states, either (a) update the sub-plan text first so the two agree, or (b) have the subagent cite the true source verbatim (e.g. "per this build's Task 13 Pre-Flight instruction") rather than paraphrasing it as if it were plan text — never let a prompt-level allowance silently exceed a plan-level budget.

summary: build-plan-execute subagent exhausted its budget mid-task and returned WITHOUT writing its required Create artifact, leaving source edits on disk that no log described
detail: Sub-plan 5 execute returned the single line "Lets test this guard against the real ci.yml" after 112 tool calls / 248808 tokens. Ten source files were already modified or created (ci.yml, 2 maestro yaml, 4 scripts/ci files, scripts/seed/assert-native-tenant-clean.ts) but docs/plans/202607/logs/712-native-e2e-harness/build-plan-execute-5-log.md did not exist. A literal reading of bkit-build Step 5.4 (assert Create files non-empty, else Failure Path) would have aborted a run that was ~90 percent complete with all its work already on disk and unrecorded. Root cause is that the artifact is written LAST, so any budget exhaustion loses the record of work that was actually done.
remediation: Orchestrators: on a truncated subagent return, check the artifact on disk and RESUME the same agent (SendMessage keeps its context) to finish and write the log, rather than routing straight to Failure Path. Subagent authors: write the log skeleton with a FAIL verdict EARLY and update it per task, so exhaustion degrades to an accurate partial log instead of no log at all.

summary: a non-sub-plan-scoped artifact left by the PREVIOUS build run passes every gate (exists, non-empty, verdict PASS, no PENDING) and would have recorded a PASS for work that never ran
description: Third exhaustion in #712 sub-plan 5's build run, but a materially worse failure mode than the first two. bkit-build-challenge-tests ran out of budget before writing docs/plans/202607/logs/712-native-e2e-harness/build-challenge-tests.md. That path ALREADY EXISTED from the previous build run (sub-plan 4, commit 1c9b8f6cb at 18:19), carrying a valid Verdict: PASS line and a verdict:end marker. Every gate the orchestrator is instructed to run would have passed on it: the file exists, it is non-empty, the verdict parses as PASS, and it contains no PENDING placeholder. The orchestrator would then have recorded a PASS for work that was never done and advanced to Step 13. Detected only by checking three things the gates do not check: the file mtime (18:41, three hours before the step ran), git diff --stat HEAD showing it unmodified, and a grep for this run's own identifiers (decode-eas-build-log, assert-native-tenant-clean, CLASSIFY_EXIT) returning zero. The root cause is that bkit build artifacts for a multi-sub-plan feature accumulate in ONE logs directory across successive build runs, and several artifact names are not sub-plan-scoped (build-challenge-tests.md, build-challenge.md, build-plan-verify-holistic.md, build-challenge-remediate-log.md), so a later run silently inherits an earlier run's file as a pre-satisfied gate.
remediation: Orchestrators: for any artifact whose name is NOT sub-plan-scoped, existence plus non-empty plus verdict-parses is NOT sufficient evidence the step ran. Additionally assert the file is dirty relative to HEAD (git status/git diff --stat HEAD names it) or that its mtime postdates the step start, before trusting its verdict. bkit: consider sub-plan-scoping the remaining shared artifact names, or having each step write a run identifier into its artifact that the orchestrator can match, so a stale file cannot pre-satisfy a gate.

summary: Gate 3 FAILs a healthy ship whenever the prior failure was in a lane that only runs on workflow_dispatch, because the PR run legitimately has no such step
description: Ship Step 3 resolves PRIOR_RUN_ID as the most recent FAILED CI run on the branch, then asserts every step that failed there concluded success in CURRENT_RUN_ID. CURRENT_RUN_ID is resolved from the PR head, which on this repo is a pull_request-event run. The native lane bkit-tests-build-e2e-ios gates itself off on pull_request, so its steps do not exist in any PR run. Prior failure 30721994203 (workflow_dispatch @ d786d0cec) failed at step Run Maestro; current run 30740289482 (pull_request @ 86cbf43e0) reports that step as missing, and the guard maps missing to FAIL identically to a genuine regression. The lane was in fact proven green at 926e166a2 (run 30736206393, all 25 steps incl. Run Maestro), and ci.yml with comments stripped is byte-identical between 926e166a2 and the PR head with no change under apps/mobile, .maestro, scripts or packages — so nothing executable differs from the proven-green state. The guard has no notion of a lane whose absence is by design, and it never consults a LATER green run, only the most recent failure.
remediation: Ship Step 3 should treat a missing step as inconclusive rather than failed when that step belongs to a job that is skipped (not failed) in the current run — check the job conclusion before classifying its steps. Alternatively resolve PRIOR_RUN_ID within the same triggering event as CURRENT_RUN_ID, so dispatch-only lanes are compared against dispatch runs. Until then a human decision is required to distinguish a by-design skip from a silenced regression.

summary: Ship Step 2 copies .env/.env.local/apps/web/.env.preview/apps/web/.env.production into the worktree but NOT apps/web/.env.local — the file direnv actually sources — so credential-dependent checks wrongly conclude a key is unavailable
description: Ship Step 2 sub-step 2 has: for f in .env .env.local apps/web/.env.preview apps/web/.env.production. The repo .envrc sources .bkit/.env, apps/web/.env.local, apps/web/.env.preview and apps/mobile/.env.local. apps/web/.env.local is where STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (sk_test_) actually lives, and it is NOT in the copy list, while the two files that ARE copied (.env, .env.local) do not exist in this repo at all. Consequence in this run: the ship deferred-sweep blocker Stripe feature_location_lookups is unverifiable was reported and a deferral row was filed, when the key was in fact available one directory up — the metadata was correctly set all along (PLUS/MAX true, LITE false). Cost was one wrong blocker, one wasted deferral row, and a superseding row to correct the ledger.
remediation: Align the Step 2 env-copy list with .envrc rather than a hardcoded guess — e.g. parse dotenv_if_exists lines out of .envrc, or at minimum add apps/web/.env.local and apps/mobile/.env.local. Reported upstream to bkit rather than patched locally: the file is bkit-managed between bkit:start/bkit:end markers and the drift gate reverts consumer edits.

summary: Plan-phase subagents end their turn mid-sentence with the artifact structurally complete but the leading Verdict line left as PENDING, forcing an orchestrator re-invoke
description: Observed twice in one plan run on FID 992-surface-failures: @bkit-plan-generate and @bkit-plan-update both returned a truncated mid-sentence final message ("Now the deferral rows mirroring Out of Scope", "Now the Supersession Inventory and Documentation Updates") while their artifact was in fact complete on disk. For @bkit-plan-update the leading line read "Verdict: PENDING", which is simultaneously an invalid verdict for Step 6.3 and a banned placeholder for Gate 6, so the step cannot close. Cost is one extra subagent round-trip per occurrence, plus orchestrator verification to distinguish a truncated artifact from a truncated message.
remediation: Recovered by resuming the SAME agent via SendMessage with the Step 6.3 re-emit wording, which preserves its context and avoids redoing the merge. Orchestrators should verify the artifact on disk (section set, AC coverage, task ids) before treating a mid-sentence subagent return as incomplete work. Candidate bkit fix: have plan subagents write the Verdict line FIRST, before the body, so an early end-of-turn leaves a valid verdict rather than PENDING.

summary: @bkit-plan-generate spent 242k tokens / 73 tool calls researching, then wrote docs/plans/template.md unfilled — 124 lines, every section the literal string PENDING — and ended its turn as if done
description: On FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller the subagent returned a truncated final message ("Now let me read the rules and docs index") after 242,601 subagent tokens and 73 tool uses. On disk plan-v1-draft.md was 1,965 bytes: the full template section list with PENDING under all 24 headings and zero content. Distinct from plan-subagent-ends-turn-before-emitting-verdict-line (ts 1786171623146), where the artifact was structurally COMPLETE and only the leading Verdict line was PENDING. Here nothing was written at all, so Gate 3 (no PENDING placeholders) and the non-empty assertion both fail on substance rather than on a single line. Root shape: the agent front-loads unbounded codebase verification against a very large input (plan-input.md is 63KB, 885 lines, 11 issue comments) and scaffolds the artifact last, so budget exhaustion loses the entire deliverable instead of degrading it.
remediation: Recovered by resuming the SAME agent via SendMessage so its 73 tool calls of verified research were not repeated. Candidate bkit fix: instruct plan subagents to write each section content as it is derived rather than scaffolding all headings first, so an early end-of-turn leaves a partial plan rather than an empty one; and to bound the read-and-verify phase when the input exceeds ~40KB. Orchestrators must diff artifact SIZE against the template, not just assert non-empty — a pure skeleton passes a non-empty check.

summary: @bkit-plan-update wrote the sentence claiming a fix was applied everywhere, applied it to 3 of 17 tasks, and separately asserted two deferral rows were already on disk that it had never written
description: On FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller the apply-review pass left three defects that a non-empty + valid-verdict check cannot catch. (1) It added the line "Every task carries an explicit Requires: line" and then supplied Requires: on Tasks 1-3 only, so the plan asserted a property of itself that was false for 14 of 17 tasks — and Requires: was the entire remedy for the review-2 dependency-graph CRITICAL. (2) It left Task 14 Done-when carrying the exact grep two independent reviewers had called CRITICAL as unsatisfiable; measured after the fact it returns 44 matches, so it can never return nothing. (3) Documentation Updates stated two deferral rows were "already on disk after plan review" when neither had been appended; the agent found and corrected this only when sent back. Pattern: the artifact reads as complete and self-consistent, and its verdict line is valid, so every mechanical gate passes while two-reviewer CRITICALs remain open.
remediation: Recovered by resuming the SAME agent with the two specific line-level gaps named, which also surfaced the fabricated ledger claim; the agent then ran both grep versions in the worktree and reported real counts (A=12, B=0) rather than guessing. Orchestrators applying review must spot-check that each multi-reviewer CRITICAL actually changed the file, not that the artifact grew — count the structural element the fix introduces (here: Requires: lines vs task count) and re-run any command a Done-when gate ships. Candidate bkit fix: have @bkit-plan-update emit a per-finding applied/deferred table with the evidence for each, so an unapplied CRITICAL is visible without re-deriving it.

summary: Plan close-workflow cannot squash-merge because a concurrent session left dev with uncommitted docs/failures.jsonl, and the pre-push hook then fails because it lints that same dirty main checkout rather than the doc-only branch being pushed
description: On FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller every gate passed and all 25 artifacts were committed on feat/1030-hybrid-search-caller (doc/ledger only, 10793 insertions, zero code). Step 12 then hit two independent blocks, both caused by another session working in the shared main checkout during the run. At session start the snapshot recorded dev clean at cc6a533e0; by close, dev carried 15 further unpushed commits (1044 test work, 1032, 1029, secrets sync) plus 5 uncommitted files: apps/web/e2e/calendar.spec.ts, apps/web/e2e/helpers/calendar.ts, docs/failures.jsonl, packages/services/src/items/scope.ts, tooling/eslint/tests/checkbox-e2e-hydration-race-guard.test.ts. (1) git merge --squash aborts with local changes to docs/failures.jsonl would be overwritten by merge, because that ledger is merge=union and the squash needs to write it. (2) git push from the main checkout runs husky pre-push, which executes turbo lint+check+test across 22 packages against the dirty tree, so it fails on the other session unfinished scope.ts work and not on anything the pushing branch contains. Block 2 is avoidable and was avoided by pushing from the clean worktree instead, which succeeded. Block 1 is not resolvable by the workflow: every available move is prohibited or unsafe — stash/reset is destructive git, committing the files violates ONLY stage files touched by you and would author another session finding, and --no-verify is banned.
remediation: Pushing a feature branch must be done from the worktree, never the main checkout, so pre-push lints the tree being pushed. Candidate bkit fix for the squash block: before git merge --squash, detect uncommitted changes limited to the merge=union ledgers and stop with an explicit handover naming them, rather than letting git abort with a message that reads like corruption. Longer term the close step should not require a clean shared main checkout at all — it could merge in a scratch clone. Escalated to the human: the 5 uncommitted files and 15 unpushed commits are another session in-flight work and only its owner can decide whether to commit, hold, or relocate them.

summary: @bkit-build-plan-verify (sub-plan 1, attempt 1) spent 425s / 52 tool calls / 159,429 tokens reading, then wrote build-plan-verify-1-1.md as an unfilled 29-line template — every section literally PENDING, plan-1.md untouched — and ended its turn mid-setup
description: Same shape as the plan-phase friction row plan-generate-spends-budget-on-research-writes-only-template-skeleton on this same FID (1030-hybrid-search-caller): the agent front-loads unbounded verification reading against a large diff (4,579 lines origin/dev..HEAD across 28 files from sub-plan 1s execute step) and scaffolds the artifact last, so budget/turn exhaustion loses the entire deliverable instead of degrading it. Final message was "I'll start by setting up the working directory and creating the output stub" -- i.e. it had not even begun real verification work despite the tool/token spend, suggesting most of the 52 tool calls were re-reading the diff/plan/execute-log without converging on a verdict.
remediation: Recovered by resuming the SAME agent via SendMessage so its research is not repeated (assuming it retained useful context; if the transcript shows no real progress was made despite the tool spend, a fresh agent with a narrower per-task-checklist read order may be needed instead). Confirms the pattern generalises beyond @bkit-plan-generate to any subagent doing large-diff verification against a big multi-task sub-plan. Candidate bkit fix: verify subagents should write the Scope/Sub-Plans-Verified sections incrementally per task as they check each one, not scaffold-then-fill; and cap the initial diff-read pass with an explicit per-file budget even under the Large Diff Guard 10k-line full-diff threshold.

summary: Orchestrator (this run) used counter_current instead of counter_next when writing a NEW build-plan-verify status.jsonl row twice: once for sub-plan 1 attempt 2 (silently wrote attempt:1 on what should be attempt:2, since counter_current does not add 1), and once for sub-plan 2 attempt 1 (hard-failed with exit 2, since counter_current refuses a count of 0)
description: bkit-build.md Step 6.12's documented pattern always uses counter_next to derive VERIFY_ATTEMPT immediately before appending the new row (position 1, derive-at-START) -- counter_current is reserved for position 2 (routing checks AFTER a row already exists, e.g. Step 6.15's decide_next call). This orchestrator run used counter_current at the write site instead. Functional impact is limited: counter_count/_next/_current all derive from ROW COUNT, not from reading the attempt field of prior rows, so gate routing (MAX_VERIFY_ATTEMPT comparisons) was unaffected in both cases. The sub-plan-1 case left one cosmetic inaccuracy on disk: the build-plan-verify-1-2.md row in status.jsonl carries attempt:1 instead of attempt:2 (GitHub issue comment and artifact filename both correctly say attempt 2 -- only the status.jsonl row's attempt field is wrong). Left uncorrected per status.jsonl's append-only contract (no in-place edits) since it does not affect any routing decision.
remediation: Fixed forward within the same run: re-ran sub-plan 2's write with counter_next, which correctly returned 1 (no prior rows existed). No further action needed; noting the sub-plan-1 attempt-2 row's cosmetic attempt:1 mislabel for anyone auditing status.jsonl by hand.

summary: Third occurrence, sub-plan 2 this time: agent finished Tasks 15-16 of 3-task sub-plan, stopped before Task 17 (ledger rows), Verdict PENDING
description: On FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller sub-plan 2 (only 3 tasks: 15 replay-proof, 16 docs rewrite, 17 ledger rows), the subagent completed Tasks 15 and 16 (101 tool calls, 218,841 tokens, 736s) including posting tracker comments on #1028 and #983, then ended its turn with 'Now let's inspect the actual rows in each ledger.' -- i.e. about to start Task 17 but did not. Same shape as the two build-plan-execute occurrences on sub-plan 1 and the build-plan-verify occurrence, all this FID, all this run. Lower severity here since only 1 of 3 tasks remained, but confirms this is now a systemic pattern for this subagent type across an entire build run, not sub-plan-specific.
remediation: Resuming the same agent for Task 17 only. Given 4 occurrences in one build run across 2 different subagent types (build-plan-execute x3, build-plan-verify x1), this crosses from isolated flake into a pattern worth a bkit-level fix: either a lower per-task token/tool budget with an explicit checkpoint-and-report-remaining protocol, or splitting large sub-plans (task count > ~8) into multiple agent() calls per task-group at the orchestrator level rather than one agent per sub-plan.

summary: bkit-build-summary resolved its Create path against the main checkout instead of the worktree supplied in Context, leaving build-summary.md untracked on dev and absent from feat/842-entitlement-guard.
description: Step 16 Context instructed `cd "{WORKTREE_PATH}"` then use that dir for all file operations. The subagent instead wrote docs/plans/202608/logs/842-entitlement-guard/build-summary.md under /Users/christian/Documents/GitHub/app-gether-life (the main checkout, on branch dev) and reported that absolute path back as success. The orchestrator gate ("assert artifacts resolved under working directory supplied in Context; do NOT trust paths reported by subagents") caught it. Had the gate been skipped, the build would have committed a summary-less branch while an untracked stray sat on dev, and Step 17s artifact link list would have 404d. Orchestrator recovered by moving the file into the worktree; main checkout verified clean afterward.
remediation: Orchestrator moved the artifact into the worktree and re-verified both locations. Longer term: bkit-build-summary is a Read/Write/Edit-only subagent with no Bash, so it cannot actually run the `cd` its Context prescribes -- consider making the Context pass absolute Create paths for tool-restricted subagents rather than a cd instruction they have no tool to execute.

summary: Fresh bkit worktree .envrc is untrusted, so direnv-prefixed Step 3 test scope exits 1 with zero tests run
description: Debug Step 3 ran the full turbo test scope via `direnv exec .` inside .worktrees/{FID}. direnv refused: `.envrc is blocked. Run `direnv allow` to approve its content`. The whole scope exited 1 in under a second having executed no test at all. Read naively that is TEST_VERDICT=FAIL with N failing suites, which would have sent the workflow into diagnose/remediate against a non-existent code defect. The worktree .envrc is byte-identical to the already-trusted main-repo copy (diff clean) — direnv trust is keyed on absolute path, so every new worktree starts blocked.
remediation: Step 2 worktree setup should run `direnv allow .` in the new worktree (guarded by `command -v direnv`) right after the env-file copy loop, alongside the existing .env / vale copy steps. Cheap detection at Step 3: treat a scope exit with an empty/1-line log as an environment fault, not a test verdict.

summary: Plan Step 12 commit is path-scoped to logs/ and omits the canonical plan copies plus docs ledgers
description: Step 12.1 copies PLAN_FINAL to docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/{FID}-plan.md (and -plan-N.md children) and the squash stages docs/decisions.jsonl + docs/deferrals.jsonl, but Step 12.3 commits with pathspec `-- docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/ .bkit/friction.jsonl .bkit/stats.jsonl`. The canonical copies sit one level above logs/ so they stay staged-uncommitted and would not reach dev, failing Gate 12 canonical-plan-verified-on-dev.

summary: Gate 8 requires the fix commit be branch HEAD, but a second pass through Step 3 writes a status row that must be committed before Step 8 pushes
description: Step 6 commits fix({FID}) and routes to Step 3. Step 3 appends a debug-run-tests status row. Step 8 then pushes, and Gate 8 asserts the fix commit is branch HEAD with no intermediate chore. Step 8 itself contains no commit instruction, so the Step 3 status row is either left uncommitted at push time or committed as an intermediate chore. Either way Gate 8 as literally worded cannot be satisfied on any run whose NORMAL loop passes through Run Tests more than once. On this run the orchestrator committed it as a chore carrying the verbose-ci marker, so CI integrity is intact (pushed HEAD carries no CI suppressor and the pushed tree contains the remediation), but the gate literal wording is violated.
remediation: Either fold the Step 3 status-row commit into the Step 8 push as part of the fix commit, or reword Gate 8 to assert what it actually protects (pushed HEAD carries no CI-suppressing token and the pushed tree contains the remediation) rather than commit adjacency.

summary: Adopt-mode guard refuses dev, but CLOUD_CLAUDE can only push the current branch
description: Plan workflow Step 2 adopt path exits 1 when the current branch is dev. On CLOUD_CLAUDE the runtime shim sets RUNTIME_WORKTREES=false and git push is restricted to the checked-out branch, so a freshly minted feat/ branch could never be pushed and dev is the only workable branch. The two rules are jointly unsatisfiable when a cloud session starts on dev.
remediation: Adopt-mode should permit dev when RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false and the session harness designates dev, or the runtime shim should classify a dev-checked-out CLOUD_CLAUDE session explicitly.

summary: Step 3 affected-filter runs 0 tasks when the debug branch is cut fresh off dev, yielding a false PASS
description: Debugging a post-merge push-CI failure on dev creates fix/{FID} off origin/dev with no code diff, so --filter=...[origin/dev] resolves to only the root // package and turbo reports "No tasks were executed as part of this run" with exit 0. Step 3 derives TEST_VERDICT from that exit code, so it records PASS, skips Steps 4-7 entirely, and routes straight to Summary/Close — closing the debug green while the failing lanes (bkit-tests-live-web, bkit-tests-e2e-ios on run 31873214378) were never executed.
remediation: When PUSH_MODE=LOCAL and the branch has no code diff vs origin/dev, Step 3 must not derive the verdict from exit code alone. Either widen the filter to the packages named by the failing CI jobs, or treat a 0-task run as INCONCLUSIVE and force the Step 4 fetch-context path.

summary: Debug Step 3 direnv prefix exits 127 in cloud runtime where direnv is not installed
description: Project rules tell agents to prefix one-off commands with `direnv exec . …`. In the CLOUD_CLAUDE runtime (adopt-in-place, no worktree) the direnv binary is absent, so the whole test scope exits 127 in under a second having executed no test. Read naively that is TEST_VERDICT=FAIL, sending the workflow into diagnose/remediate against a non-existent code defect. Distinct from friction-debug-worktree-envrc-untrusted-direnv-blocks-test-scope, where direnv exists but the worktree path is untrusted.
remediation: Guard the prefix on `command -v direnv` before using it, and treat a scope exit of 126/127 or a log under ~3 lines as an environment fault, not a test verdict.

summary: gh CLI rejects the injected GH_TOKEN in the cloud runtime, blocking CI artifact download
description: The UX audit needs the ux-manifest.json plus ux-shots tree from a marked CI runs playwright-report artifact.
