summary: second occurrence — a subagent exhausted its budget and left a Verdict: PENDING skeleton, the exact placeholder its own gate forbids
description: Second occurrence in the same build run (#712 sub-plan 5). First: build-plan-execute returned a one-line fragment with NO artifact after 112 tool calls. Second: build-plan-verify (holistic) returned "Now let me read the master plan..." after 54 tool calls, having written only a 29-line skeleton whose verdict block read "Verdict: PENDING" — the exact string the orchestrator gate forbids. Both were resumed successfully via SendMessage with context intact, so the work was not lost, but a literal reading of the bkit-build gates (assert Create files non-empty; no PENDING placeholders remain) would have routed BOTH to the Failure Path and aborted a healthy run. The common shape: the agent writes its artifact LAST (or writes a placeholder skeleton early and fills it in at the end), so budget exhaustion destroys the record rather than degrading it.
remediation: Orchestrators: treat a truncated subagent return as "incomplete", not "failed" — check the artifact on disk, and if it is missing or still carries a PENDING placeholder, RESUME the same agent with SendMessage (its context survives) before considering the Failure Path. Subagent authors: write the verdict block with a conservative FAIL/CONCERNS value early and revise it as findings land, so exhaustion degrades to an accurate partial artifact instead of a forbidden placeholder or nothing at all.

summary: bkit-build-plan-execute for sub-plan 1/2 stopped after Task 8 of 14, left Verdict: PENDING, final message mid-sentence
description: On FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller sub-plan 1 (14 tasks), the subagent completed Tasks 1-8 (migration, local apply, typegen, SQL mirror sync, 2 new integration suites, #384 hardening extension) across 103 tool calls / 226,343 subagent tokens / 838s, partially started Task 9 (edited hybrid-search.ts source but not its unit test hybrid-search.test.ts), and ended its turn with the literal final message "Now let's update its unit test suite." build-plan-execute-1-log.md was left with Verdict: PENDING and only 8 of 14 tasks logged. Same shape as the plan-phase friction rows plan-generate-spends-budget-on-research-writes-only-template-skeleton and plan-subagent-ends-turn-before-emitting-verdict-line on this same FID — budget/turn exhaustion on a large multi-task sub-plan loses the tail of the tasklist.
remediation: Recovered by resuming the SAME agent (not a fresh one) via SendMessage, so the 103 already-completed tool calls covering Tasks 1-8 are not re-run; instructed it to finish Task 9's test suite through Task 14 and emit a real PASS/FAIL verdict. Candidate bkit fix: bkit-build-plan-execute should write/update the execution log incrementally after each task (already does) but also self-checkpoint remaining task count against a token/turn budget and hand back a CONCERNS verdict with an explicit remaining-tasks list rather than trailing off mid-sentence, so the orchestrator does not have to diff git status against the plan file to discover the gap.

summary: Second occurrence same run: resumed agent got through Tasks 9-13 (100 more tool calls, 333,514 tokens, 649s) then stopped again mid-Task 14 with Verdict still PENDING

Let's start with the three search-items* integration tests.' Verdict line still literally PENDING. summary: Fifth occurrence this run, different subagent type: @bkit-build-summary ended its turn mid-investigation (checking whether commit hashes ef9a49516/d82e92472 exist) before writing build-summary.md at all -- zero bytes on disk, not even a template stub

The subagent spent 25 tool calls / 53,401 tokens / 84s investigating whether those hashes were real (git log, git objects directory) before writing anything, then ended its turn with 'Let me search for the mentioned commit hashes in the git log. Given five occurrences across the same run and now four distinct subagent types, this is no longer edge-case flakiness -- worth a bkit-level fix (see the four earlier friction rows this run with the same key for candidate fixes: incremental artifact writes, per-task budget checkpoints, or splitting oversized single-agent-single-artifact steps).

summary: Second confirmed occurrence (first was #842, ts 1786516771000): @bkit-build-summary again resolved its Create path against the main checkout instead of the worktree, this time on FID 1030-hybrid-search-caller, and its own final report also described only sub-plan 1 as if sub-plan 2 had not happened
description: Same root cause as the #842 row: bkit-build-summary has Read/Write/Edit tools only, no Bash, so the Context's `cd "{WORKTREE_PATH}"` instruction is physically un-executable by this subagent -- it has no tool that performs cd. The first invocation this run wrote docs/plans/202608/logs/1030-hybrid-search-caller/build-summary.md under /Users/christian/Documents/GitHub/app-gether-life (main checkout, branch dev) and reported that path back as success; caught by the orchestrator gate (assert artifacts resolved under working directory supplied in Context). A second, fresh invocation (not a resume) with explicit absolute paths for every Read/Create target plus an inlined ground-truth summary of the full build state produced a correct artifact in the correct location.

The prior #842 row's suggested fix stands and is now confirmed by a second occurrence: bkit-build-summary's Context should pass absolute Create/Read paths directly rather than a cd instruction, since this subagent class structurally cannot cd.

summary: Step 17 CI-Dispatch Gate: push/PR-triggered CI dispatch silently no-op'd on PR 847, same symptom as build-843-push-triggered-ci-dispatch-silent-no-op (root cause was unconfirmed there); this time root-caused.
description: feat/561-mcp-server-connector's history includes an early commit (Step 2 worktree-setup) whose message carries a skip-ci-class token. Every push/PR-synchronize event for this branch dispatched zero Actions runs (confirmed via gh api actions/runs — zero entries for the branch across 3 pushes with CLEAN HEAD messages), while gh workflow run ci.yml (workflow_dispatch) worked instantly and repeatedly. The repo's own .husky/pre-push hook independently encodes the same class of guard (HEAD-only skip-ci check + open-PR probe), but that only checks the CURRENT HEAD commit message, not history — so it did not (and structurally cannot) catch a marker buried earlier in a branch's commits. This strongly suggests GitHub's native pull_request-trigger skip-ci evaluation is NOT scoped to only the newest commit for a multi-commit push/PR (contrary to the docs' single-commit framing), consistent with this repo's own documented squash-merge trap (reference_squash_release_skip_ci_trap) but now also observed on a live open PR pre-merge, not just at squash time.
remediation: Recovered via two manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>` dispatches (first caught 2 real bugs, second confirmed green post-fix). No rebase was attempted (git rebase -i is prohibited for this orchestrator) so the underlying poisoned commit remains in this PR's history; native dispatch will likely stay suppressed for the life of this PR. If this recurs, consider: (a) a build-workflow step that greps ALL new commits (not just HEAD) for skip-ci tokens BEFORE the first push and blocks/rewords early, since [skip ci] is only appropriate on doc-only/status commits when no PR will ever be opened from that branch; (b) a documented manual-dispatch fallback in the Step 17 CI-Dispatch Gate itself for this exact symptom, rather than rediscovering it per-PR.

description: @bkit-plan-update stopped mid-queue with `Verdict: PENDING` still in the header after ~50 tool calls, having applied 10 of 14 findings. The artifact looked complete (105KB, full structure, coherent tail), so the orchestrator spot-checked four findings (A, B, D, G-atomicity), found them landed, and resumed the agent with `Do NOT redo work` + a verdict-only instruction. That premise was WRONG: findings F (CRITICAL, would red bkit-tests-check on every run), G-mirror (CRITICAL), M1 and M5 were still unapplied. The subagent audited on-disk state, rejected the orchestrator premise, finished the four, and only then emitted PASS.
recovery: Subagent self-corrected — it refused to certify PASS over an unapplied CRITICAL and completed the queue instead of obeying the (wrong) do-not-redo instruction. Orchestrator re-verified the late fixes against live source (the 9-key env enumeration matches ci.yml:879-888 exactly) and confirmed the commit captured the completed state. No rework lost; no bad verdict shipped.
lesson: A PENDING verdict means the agent did not finish its QUEUE, not merely its header — the artifact being large, well-structured and coherent is NOT evidence the finding queue drained. The Step 5.3 `Do NOT redo work` re-emit instruction is only safe once EVERY finding is confirmed applied; a 4-of-14 spot-check cannot establish that. Either verify all findings before re-emitting, or resume WITHOUT the do-not-redo constraint and let the agent audit its own queue.

description: Orchestrator self-inflicted a wasted CI cycle. While run 29454200201 (the first real test of THREE unproven changes at once — node_modules cache removal, sequential E2E lanes, and @live running parallel to e2e) was in flight and being actively monitored, the orchestrator committed and pushed a DOCS-ONLY change (a failures.jsonl ledger row). The PR's concurrency group cancelled 29454200201 mid-run and started 29454436704 on the new HEAD. Net effect: ~10 minutes of CI wall-clock burned for nothing, on a branch whose entire purpose is REDUCING CI wall-clock, and the awaited measurement was delayed by a full cycle. The push itself was not wrong — the ledger row and the #681 correction comment were both worth recording — the error was pushing it DURING an in-flight run instead of holding it until the run reported, or batching it into the next code push.
recovery: None available — a cancelled run cannot be resumed. The new run 29454436704 carries the identical tree plus the docs row, so the measurement is delayed rather than lost. Re-pointed the monitor at the new run id.
lesson: Never push to a branch while a run you are waiting on is in flight — a PR push cancels the in-progress run via the concurrency group. Ledger/docs writes that are not needed by CI should be held in the working tree (or committed but NOT pushed) until the awaited run reports, then batched with the next real change. This matters most in exactly this situation: several unproven changes landing together, where the pending run is the only thing that can tell you which of them works. Cheap check before any `git push`: `gh run list --branch <b> --limit 1 --json status` — if it is in_progress and you care about its result, wait.

description: Four subagents terminated mid-flight and had to be resumed: @bkit-plan-generate (soft-truncated its final message), @bkit-plan-update apply-review (API error 'Connection closed mid-response'), @bkit-plan-scope-check-2 (stopped with NO artifact on disk at all), @bkit-plan-update apply-scope (stopped mid-edit of the ledger sub-header). In three of the four cases the agent left an artifact that looked plausible but carried 'Verdict: PENDING' at line 1 — a completion claim the workflow gate would reject. scope-check-2 wrote nothing despite reporting verification work in-context.
recovery: Orchestrator verified every artifact on disk (line count, verdict header, PENDING grep, git status, ledger numstat) before accepting any subagent completion claim, per the repo rule 'verify subagent artifact before trusting completion'. Each cut-off agent was resumed via SendMessage with its context intact rather than restarted from scratch — resumes were given an explicit inventory of what was already verified done (so they would not redo work), an explicit list of what remained, and a mandatory 'cd back into the worktree, verify with pwd' first instruction (resumed agents can lose cwd). lesson: A subagent's final message is not evidence of completion — three of four cut-off agents left a plausible-looking artifact stamped 'Verdict: PENDING', and one left no file at all while reporting progress. Always check disk. Resume-with-inventory (naming what is verified-done and what remains) is materially cheaper than re-running a 150K-token subagent, and preserved correctness across all four incidents here.

summary: Gate 3 FAILs a healthy ship whenever the prior failure was in a lane that only runs on workflow_dispatch, because the PR run legitimately has no such step
description: Ship Step 3 resolves PRIOR_RUN_ID as the most recent FAILED CI run on the branch, then asserts every step that failed there concluded success in CURRENT_RUN_ID. CURRENT_RUN_ID is resolved from the PR head, which on this repo is a pull_request-event run. The native lane bkit-tests-build-e2e-ios gates itself off on pull_request, so its steps do not exist in any PR run. Prior failure 30721994203 (workflow_dispatch @ d786d0cec) failed at step Run Maestro; current run 30740289482 (pull_request @ 86cbf43e0) reports that step as missing, and the guard maps missing to FAIL identically to a genuine regression. The lane was in fact proven green at 926e166a2 (run 30736206393, all 25 steps incl. Run Maestro), and ci.yml with comments stripped is byte-identical between 926e166a2 and the PR head with no change under apps/mobile, .maestro, scripts or packages — so nothing executable differs from the proven-green state. The guard has no notion of a lane whose absence is by design, and it never consults a LATER green run, only the most recent failure.
remediation: Ship Step 3 should treat a missing step as inconclusive rather than failed when that step belongs to a job that is skipped (not failed) in the current run — check the job conclusion before classifying its steps. Alternatively resolve PRIOR_RUN_ID within the same triggering event as CURRENT_RUN_ID, so dispatch-only lanes are compared against dispatch runs. Until then a human decision is required to distinguish a by-design skip from a silenced regression.

summary: Fresh bkit worktree .envrc is untrusted, so direnv-prefixed Step 3 test scope exits 1 with zero tests run
description: Debug Step 3 ran the full turbo test scope via `direnv exec .` inside .worktrees/{FID}. direnv refused: `.envrc is blocked. Run `direnv allow` to approve its content`. The whole scope exited 1 in under a second having executed no test at all. Read naively that is TEST_VERDICT=FAIL with N failing suites, which would have sent the workflow into diagnose/remediate against a non-existent code defect. The worktree .envrc is byte-identical to the already-trusted main-repo copy (diff clean) — direnv trust is keyed on absolute path, so every new worktree starts blocked.
remediation: Step 2 worktree setup should run `direnv allow .` in the new worktree (guarded by `command -v direnv`) right after the env-file copy loop, alongside the existing .env / vale copy steps. Cheap detection at Step 3: treat a scope exit with an empty/1-line log as an environment fault, not a test verdict.

summary: Gate 8 requires the fix commit be branch HEAD, but a second pass through Step 3 writes a status row that must be committed before Step 8 pushes
description: Step 6 commits fix({FID}) and routes to Step 3. Step 3 appends a debug-run-tests status row. Step 8 then pushes, and Gate 8 asserts the fix commit is branch HEAD with no intermediate chore. Step 8 itself contains no commit instruction, so the Step 3 status row is either left uncommitted at push time or committed as an intermediate chore. Either way Gate 8 as literally worded cannot be satisfied on any run whose NORMAL loop passes through Run Tests more than once. On this run the orchestrator committed it as a chore carrying the verbose-ci marker, so CI integrity is intact (pushed HEAD carries no CI suppressor and the pushed tree contains the remediation), but the gate literal wording is violated.
remediation: Either fold the Step 3 status-row commit into the Step 8 push as part of the fix commit, or reword Gate 8 to assert what it actually protects (pushed HEAD carries no CI-suppressing token and the pushed tree contains the remediation) rather than commit adjacency.

remediation: Guard the prefix on `command -v direnv` before using it, and treat a scope exit of 126/127 or a log under ~3 lines as an environment fault, not a test verdict.

summary: gh CLI rejects the injected GH_TOKEN in the cloud runtime, blocking CI artifact download
description: The UX audit needs the ux-manifest.json plus ux-shots tree from a marked CI runs playwright-report artifact. In the cloud runtime gh auth status reports "The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid", so gh run download is unavailable, and the GitHub MCP server exposes no actions/artifact tools (no list_workflow_runs, no download_workflow_run_artifact) — the documented gh route and the MCP route are both dead ends.
remediation: Fetch the artifact over the REST API with curl using the proxy-injected bearer token (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs?head_sha=… then /actions/artifacts/{id}/zip), which authenticates where the gh CLI does not. Unzip results/ux-manifest.json and results/ux-shots into apps/web/playwright/results so manifest-relative shot paths resolve.
